For the first two miles there were 15 walkers grouped together at the front including Len, John and just hanging on at no. 15, Carl. With mile times being given it became obvious that the speed was rather excessive for some of those in the group, and slowly they peeled off as
John seemed further back than usual, he was taking things easy in case a previous injury flared up. It looked as if there would be no medals this time.
John had passed Graham and put in a strong finish to record a personal best. The team was completed by a powerfully finishing John Bromley to give us a good win.

John put up a personal best to keep us in the reckoning for a place (Sheffield already had their team home and dry). It seemed a while before Ron appeared in a small group, he too put in a great effort round the track, and although he just failed to beat three hours recorded a p.b.

John was in good form and soon appeared and it was not long before Ray came in to give us another team win. Shortly before the hour was up Trevor McDermott crossed the line - only 16 years of age and '7 in the hour' in his first season.
Carl was in the leading group with John well placed and it wasn't long before Allan came through with Ray moving strongly to complete our four.
